podcast.title: "All the Small Things" Inspiration
podcast.body: He personally wrote the hit song "All the Small Things" for his then-girlfriend, Jennifer, with the specific intention of creating a catchy and commercially successful track. "All the small things, Tom DeLong wrote that for his girlfriend, Jennifer."

podcast.title: Childhood and Skater Identity
podcast.body: Growing up in the San Diego suburb of Poe, Tom DeLong was described as a solid C student and a "menace" on his skateboard, frequently chasing people off sidewalks throughout the city. "Tom DeLong is from the San Diego suburb of Poe. When he was a kid, a solid C student, he was a menace on his skateboard, chasing people off sidewalks from one end of the city to the other."

podcast.title: First Guitar and Performance
podcast.body: After receiving a new guitar for his birthday, he decided to perform a solo acoustic song titled "Who's Gonna Shave Your Back" under the moniker "Big Oily Men" at a battle of the bands event organized by Rancho Bernardo. "And Tom had just got a new guitar for his birthday and he thought he'd give it a whirl."

podcast.title: Trumpet Playing
podcast.body: Despite no apparent musical talent for it, his parents bought him a trumpet, which he used to wake his family early in the morning with a "bad rendition of Reveley before dawn." "For some reason, his parents bought him a trumpet, which he then used to wake the family with a bad rendition of Reveley before dawn."

xref.title: Estrangement from Blink 182 (2005-2022)
xref.body: Following Blink 182's indefinite hiatus in 2005, Tom DeLonge and Mark Hoppus did not communicate for years. He notably quit Blink 182 twice, the second time in early 2015, either to focus on non-musical projects or due to an unwillingness to sign a contract requiring sole focus on the band. He remained estranged from Mark and Travis through 2021. "Tom DeLong and bass player Mark Hoppiz did not talk for years."

xref.title: Estrangement from Tom DeLonge (2005-2022)
xref.body: After Blink 182's indefinite hiatus began in 2005, Mark Hoppus and Tom DeLonge did not speak to each other for several years. "Tom DeLong and bass player Mark Hoppiz did not talk for years."

xref.title: Disagreement over Major Label Deal
xref.body: He strongly believed that signing with MCA, a major label, constituted a "very unpunk move," creating significant friction and disagreement within the band, particularly with Mark Hoppas and Tom DeLong who were supportive of the deal. "Scott? Not so much. He thought that signing with MCA was a very unpunk move."

xref.title: Fired from Blink-182
xref.body: In May 1998, despite agreeing to enter rehab, Tom DeLong and Mark Hoppas felt that Scott's behavior was negatively impacting the band's performances, leading to his dismissal. While some accounts suggest he was fired over the phone, he was ultimately replaced by Travis Barker. "So Scott was fired. Some story said he was fired over the phone, but whatever the case is, he was out and Travis was in."

xref.title: Initial Meeting with Tom DeLong
xref.body: Scott Rainer, a drummer whose current band was "falling apart," was drawn to Tom DeLong's solo acoustic performance at a local battle of the bands. He later met Tom at a party, which eventually led to their musical collaboration. "And this attracted the attention of a drummer named Scott Rainer who was in a band that was in the process of falling apart."

xref.title: Post-Blink-182 UFO Research Career
xref.body: After leaving Blink-182, Tom DeLonge embarked on a full-time career as a UFO researcher. He is dedicated to uncovering and exposing what he believes is a vast government conspiracy covering up the existence of aliens. "Tom DeLong isn't in Blink 1.2 anymore. He's working full-time as a UFO researcher and is determined to expose the vast government cover-up conspiracy of the existence of aliens."

srcs.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 60 Minutes: 2017 Edition

xref.title: Previous Bands and Connection to Tom
xref.body: Before joining Blink, Mark, who was a few years older than Tom DeLong and Scott Rainer, had already been a member of "a bunch of bands." He connected with Tom through his sister, who was dating one of Tom's friends, leading to their collaboration in songwriting. "Mark's sister was going out with one of Tom's friends, a connection was made and they started writing songs together."

xref.title: School Expulsion
xref.body: During eighth grade, he was expelled from his school after showing up drunk to a basketball game. This expulsion serendipitously led him to register at another school for a semester, a key event that ultimately connected him with Tom DeLong. "One night he showed up at his school for a basketball game. He was in grade eight and he was drunk. That got him expelled, which meant he had to register at another school for one semester."

xref.title: Tom DeLong's Financial Difficulties
xref.body: Tom DeLong and his wife faced financial troubles due to the US housing bust, trying to sell their large 6500 sq ft, 5-bathroom house in Rancho Santa Fe, California (1.1 acres in a gated community), initially listed at $8 million, then $6.25 million, and finally $5.1 million, resulting in an estimated 20% loss after renovations. "Tom DeLong and his wife have been caught up in the housing bust in the US."

xref.title: Voice Strain during Dude Ranch
xref.body: During the recording sessions for "Dude Ranch," Mark severely strained his voice by attempting to sing the album's first single, which was outside his vocal range. This injury accounts for his distinct vocal quality on the song "Dammit" and why Tom DeLong often sang the chorus when the band performed it live. "Mark had really screwed up his voice by trying to sing the first single from the song which was outside his range."
